header_summary:
DropKick, a new protocol designed to assist Bitcoin users transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) wallets, leverages blockchain's timestamping to safely commit secrets that protect against quantum computer threats. The protocol uses a commitment scheme integrated through blockchain elements like OP_RETURN or taproot tweaks, ensuring minimal blockchain impact until the reveal phase. For further details on DropKick's technical operations, visit [conduition.io](https://conduition.io/bitcoin/dropkick). 

Michael, known as fanquake, has released a new set of Bitcoin test binaries, enhancing compatibility and security across various architectures, a development crucial for maintaining high standards in Bitcoin software. This release, available on [GitHub](https://github.com/fanquake/bitcoin/releases/tag/static_bitcoind_db73d1623957), represents a significant update incorporating the latest glibc versions and offers both standard and debug versions with secure guix hashes.

A strategy to ensure encrypted outputs consistently reach 108 characters using rejection sampling has been discussed, improving security and reliability for end-users, especially in data inheritance scenarios. This method, detailed at [Delving Bitcoin](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/pq-single-address-backup-bip-38-for-p2mr-bc1z-104-char-encrypted-backup-format/2767/7), simplifies encrypted data verification and enhances user confidence without significant computational overhead. 

The adoption of the P2TRv2 protocol could potentially lead to mempool congestion and fee spikes, necessitating long-term strategic planning for blockchain scalability and security in a post-quantum world. This discussion, available at [Delving Bitcoin](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/pqc-output-type-discussion/2749/8), emphasizes the need for technological advancements and resource management to accommodate future quantum-resistant blockchain innovations.

recent_posts.title: DropKick ⚽️ - A minimal commit/reveal PQ rescue protocol
recent_posts.summary:
- DropKick aids Bitcoin users by securing transfers to PQ-secure wallets using blockchain commitments.
- It uses a minimal blockchain footprint until the reveal phase, enhancing efficiency and security.
- Unlike Tadge Dryja’s protocols, DropKick uses merkle trees for simpler, less visible commitment embedding.

recent_posts.title: Boomerang: Bitcoin Cold Storage with Built-In Coercion Resistance
recent_posts.summary: - The Boomlet is the key component lacking a backup activation mechanism.  - Plans include enhancing WT and SAR components for better fault tolerance.  - Incorporating a recovery checklist is proposed to improve disaster management.

active_posts.title: Giving teeth to expected EC disabling: P2XX(-T)(-ML)
active_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin's P2TRv2 output enhancements address future quantum threats through EC opcode disabling.
- Two proposals, Tripwire and Miner Lockdown, offer mechanisms for preemptive security measures.
- These integrations aim for user-driven consensus and robust quantum-resistant blockchain security.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Anti-Fee-Sniping with LockTime
active_posts.summary: - The nLockTime feature in Bitcoin Core and Electrum includes anti-fee-sniping since 2014 and 2017.  - BIP326 introduces nSequence in taproot transactions, shifting the protocol's approach.  - The draft BIP sets nLockTime to the blockchain tip height, adding stability to transactions.

active_posts.title: post-quantum: solution ideas to "tripwire"game-theory issues + a certificate-based rescue protocol
active_posts.summary:
- Mitigating blockchain game-theory risks uses strategies like NUMS pointwork as proof.
- Group signatures and a novel Merkle tree potentially boost blockchain resilience against quantum threats.
- Techniques include timestamping ownership proofs on the blockchain to secure against quantum decryption.

active_posts.title: Segwit commitment to post-quantum witness data?
active_posts.summary:
- Enhancing blockchain for post-quantum cryptography includes creating an extension block area.
- New transaction identifiers and block commitments are needed, complicating network infrastructure.
- An alternative involves embedding post-quantum data within segwit, keeping current identifiers intact.

active_posts.title: Running Core's real consensus code inside a zkVM
active_posts.summary:
- Hazync enhances Bitcoin consensus verification, minimizing re-execution of historical blocks.
- It utilizes a browser-based tool, allowing public, software-free proof validation.
- The system is open for community contributions and adversarial reviews to ensure robustness.

active_posts.title: Universal opt-in replay protection?
active_posts.summary: - The proposal suggests opt-in replay protection using a 34-byte Annex for forks.  - Taproot signatures committed to the annex would help users identify and adhere to specific chains.  - The mechanism aims to protect user interests and regulate miner behavior during chain splits.

today_in_history_posts.title: Do we really want users to solve an NP-hard problem when they wish to find a cheap way of paying each	other on the Lightning Network?
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Rene Pickhardt raised concerns about non-linear functions in the Lightning Network.
- ZmnSCPxj discussed NP-hard payment routing and functional package management solutions.
- He proposed a variant of Pickhardt-Richter payments for current network conditions.

today_in_history_posts.title: Eclipsing Bitcoin Nodes with BGP Interception Attacks
today_in_history_posts.summary: - A new BGP hijacking method poses significant risks to the Bitcoin network.  - Attackers can intercept Bitcoin traffic by manipulating BGP routes and using BGP communities.  - Recommended defenses include using traceroute for route-aware peer selection in Bitcoin Core.
